items.question: How long does my license last?
items.answer: LightBurn will work forever as long as you have your license key, but after a year you will need to renew the maintenance on your license to keep getting the latest features and updates.

items.question: What operating systems does your software work with?
Is LightBurn Compatible with My Laser Machine?
items.answer: LightBurn supports: Ruida (CO2), GRBL (Diode and CO2 lasers), Smoothieboard, TopWisdom, EZCad2 & EZCad2-Lite (Galvo fiber, CO2, and UV). Not sure about compatibility? Download the free trial and test it directly with your machine.

items.question: Does LightBurn Work on Windows, Mac, and Linux?
items.answer: Yes! LightBurn is compatible with Windows only, allowing you to use it on your preferred operating system. Try it risk-free – Download the 30-day free trial and see how it works on your device!

items.question: Is LightBurn a Subscription or a One-Time Purchase?
items.answer: LightBurn is a One-Time Purchase – No Monthly Subscription! When you buy LightBurn, you get lifetime access with 12 months of free updates included.

items.question: What Happens After 12 Months? Do I Need to Pay Again?
items.answer: No, you do not need to pay again. After 12 months, you can continue using LightBurn indefinitely with the last version you received. If you want to receive new updates after the first year, you can renew your license at any time, but this is completely optional.

items.question: Can my whole team use the software?
items.answer: Yes, even commercial businesses can use the same Activation across their entire team without additional costs.

items.question: How do I buy the software?
items.answer: It's easy! Just add it to your cart, fill in your details, and you'll get your Download Link right after completing your purchase.

guide.title: LightBurn installation and usage guide
guide.intro: Everything you need to get LightBurn installed, connected to your machine, and cutting your first job.

install.title: Installing LightBurn
install.intro: Work through these in order. The whole process usually takes under ten minutes.

steps.title: Check your system
steps.body: LightBurn runs on Windows 10 and Windows 11. Make sure you have administrator rights on the computer you are installing on.

steps.title: Download the installer
steps.body: Use the download link from your order email. Save the file somewhere you can find it, such as your Downloads folder.

steps.title: Run the installer
steps.body: Open the downloaded file and follow the prompts. Windows may ask you to confirm the installation; accept to continue.

steps.title: Enter your licence key
steps.body: Start LightBurn and enter the licence key from your order email when prompted. Keep that email — you will need the key again if you reinstall.

steps.title: Add your laser
steps.body: Open Devices and add your controller: Ruida, GRBL, Smoothieboard, TopWisdom or EZCad2. Set your bed size and origin to match your machine.

steps.title: Run a test
steps.body: Start with a small, low-power test on scrap material to confirm framing and focus before committing to a real job.

videos.title: Video tutorials
videos.intro: Watch the software in use before you start on your own machine.
videos.channelBody: Official tutorials covering setup, layers, camera alignment and more.

features.title: What you can do with LightBurn

items.title: Layers and settings
items.body: Give each layer its own power, speed and number of passes, so cutting, scoring and engraving run in one job.

items.title: Import your artwork
items.body: Bring in vector and image files from tools like Adobe Illustrator, CorelDRAW and CAD software.

items.title: Camera alignment
items.body: With a supported camera, line your design up against the material on the bed instead of guessing.

items.title: Preview before you burn
items.body: Simulate the whole job first and catch mistakes before they cost you material.

items.title: Wide controller support
items.body: Works with Ruida, GRBL, Smoothieboard, TopWisdom and EZCad2 controllers.

items.title: Edit without leaving
items.body: Create and adjust vector shapes directly in LightBurn, without switching to another program.
